topicName: Performance Schema and Information Schema Diagnostics
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"MySQL Performance Schema and Information Schema Diagnostics"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Diagnosing performance bottlenecks in MySQL requires a deep understanding of its internal monitoring subsystems: the Information Schema and the Performance Schema. This tutorial covers how to leverage both tools effectively for database administration and query tuning."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Information Schema vs Performance Schema"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Information Schema provides metadata about the dictionary of the database, such as table structures, column details, and index information. It acts as a read-only catalog. Conversely, the Performance Schema monitors server execution at a granular level, tracking events, mutexes, file I/O, and wait times with minimal overhead."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Querying Information Schema for Table and Index Diagnostics"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"To identify unindexed tables or examine storage usage across your database schemas, you can query the Information Schema directly."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, ROUND((DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH) / 1024 / 1024, 2) AS TOTAL_SIZE_MB FROM information_schema.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys') ORDER BY TOTAL_SIZE_MB DESC LIMIT 10;"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Enabling and Configuring Performance Schema"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, the Performance Schema is enabled in modern MySQL installations. However, specific instruments and consumers might need to be activated to capture precise diagnostics. You can check the current status using setup tables."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"UPDATE performance_schema.setup_instruments SET ENABLED = 'YES', TIMED = 'YES' WHERE NAME LIKE 'wait/io/file/%';"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Diagnosing Slow Statements with Performance Schema"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The events_statements_summary_by_digest table aggregates execution statistics for SQL statements, helping you find queries that consume the most cumulative execution time."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"SELECT DIGEST_TEXT, COUNT_STAR AS EXEC_COUNT, ROUND(SUM_TIMER_WAIT / 1000000000, 2) AS TOTAL_LATENCY_MS, ROUND(AVG_TIMER_WAIT / 1000000, 2) AS AVG_LATENCY_MS FROM performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest ORDER BY SUM_TIMER_WAIT DESC LIMIT 5;"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Identifying File I/O Bottlenecks"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Disk latency often impacts overall database performance. The file_summary_by_instance table tracks read and write operations across physical and temporary data files."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"SELECT FILE_NAME, COUNT_READ, ROUND(SUM_BY_READ_MS, 2) AS READ_MS, COUNT_WRITE, ROUND(SUM_BY_WRITE_MS, 2) AS WRITE_MS FROM performance_schema.file_summary_by_instance WHERE EVENT_NAME LIKE 'wait/io/file/sql/data%' ORDER BY SUM_BY_READ_MS DESC LIMIT 5;"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Production Diagnostics"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep Performance Schema memory consumption in check by adjusting sizing parameters in my.cnf if necessary."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use the sys schema views, which act as wrappers around Performance Schema tables for easier human interpretation."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid running heavy Information Schema queries frequently on high-traffic production servers, as they can cause metadata locks."}]
